prompt:
Workspace search shows things that were deleted and misses things that are back. Support collected these reports:

1. After an issue is archived, the issue itself no longer turns up in search, but its comments still do, and clicking one leads to an archived issue.
2. After an admin archives a whole project, the project disappears from search, but its issues and all of their comments are still found. This happens whether or not the admin chose to archive the project's issues as well. When the issues were kept, comments posted on them afterwards and edits made to them afterwards show up in search too.
3. When an archived project is restored, it never comes back in search, and neither do the issues and comments that had been kept.
4. Support ran the "rebuild search index" job for an affected workspace to clean this up. It made things worse: archived issues, deleted comments and the content of archived projects came back. In a large workspace, older issues and their comments were still missing after the rebuild. Entries that should not be there survived it.

The rule search must follow: a project can be found while it is live. An issue can be found while the issue and its project are both live. A comment can be found while the comment, its issue and that issue's project are all live. Search results and their reported total must follow this rule at all times: through archiving and restoring, and through comments and edits made at any time. Restoring a project does not restore issues that were archived, whether they were archived with the project or on their own before it, so those issues and their comments stay hidden. A rebuild of one workspace's index must leave exactly the entries the rule allows for all of that workspace's content, however large the workspace is, and it must not touch any other workspace's entries.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Root cause (shared index-maintenance layer): the search index writers (indexIssue/indexComment/indexProject in search-service, which the event listeners, the reindex_requested handler and the rebuild job all call) have no notion of searchability. They upsert whatever row they are handed, and every caller relies on its own filtering. Latent in pristine: issue.archived removes only the issue document (comments stay); project.archived removes only the project document (issues and comments stay, with or without the cascade); nothing listens to project.restored; comments/edits on live issues of an archived project are indexed; comment documents carry no project id. Injected (bug.patch, jobs layer): the rebuild job now reads projects, issues and comments with includeArchived: true, with a comment saying the writers decide what is searchable. They do not, so a rebuild resurrects archived and deleted content. It also still reads only the first page (100) of projects, issues and comments, and it never removes stale documents (latent). Reference fix (3 files, +193/-41): the rule moves into the writers (they upsert or delete per the rule; a comment checks its issue and the issue's project), plus subtree helpers syncIssueTree/syncProjectTree that walk all pages. Listeners: issue.archived removes the issue and its comments; project.archived and project.restored re-apply the rule to the whole project tree. The rebuild clears the org's documents (new search-repository deleteAllSearchDocuments, org-scoped) and pages through live projects, their live issues and their live comments. Cause and symptoms span search-service, search-repository, the reindex job, issue/project/comment services (events), the event registry, and the issue/comment/project repositories. Why hard: the obvious fix (revert includeArchived in the job) fixes only the rebuild ghosts. Fixing the listeners without the job leaves the 100-row page cap. Query-time filtering breaks the totals the test checks. Restore must re-derive state per issue and comment: individually archived issues and deleted comments stay hidden, and kept issues come back. Validation: bug -> git apply clean, tsc 0, visible 617/617; hidden 9/9 fail; bug+solution -> hidden 9/9, full 626/626, tsc 0; naive A (fix only the rebuild job: live rows, all pages, purge) -> 6/9 fail; naive B (rule in the writers + listeners, job untouched) -> 1/9 fail (large workspace); hidden x3 stable.
